builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
summary: It replaces the need to train any-order or discrete-diffusion image models from scratch by adapting existing pretrained raster-scan autoregressive models with future-aware positional embeddings and an ordering curriculum. The cost is an additional 13-33% compute relative to pretraining and a 1.2-1.9 point increase in class-conditional FID. Failure can occur if base pretrained models are unavailable, the target-position identifiability problem is not resolved, or the curriculum fails to find a stable any-order basin.
rationale: The method allows small teams to add inpainting, outpainting, and editing capabilities to existing AR image models using modest compute while retaining standard AR inference optimizations like KV caching.
technique: Unlocking any-order generation in pretrained AR image models

claims.statement: It replaces the need to train any-order or discrete-diffusion image models from scratch by adapting existing pretrained raster-scan autoregressive models with future-aware positional embeddings and an ordering curriculum. The cost is an additional 13-33% compute relative to pretraining and a 1.2-1.9 point increase in class-conditional FID. Failure can occur if base pretrained models are unavailable, the target-position identifiability problem is not resolved, or the curriculum fails to find a stable any-order basin.

Substantially outperforms MaskGIT on ImageNet inpainting (FID 6.21 vs. 10.44) and outpainting; trades a 1.2-1.9 increase in class-conditional FID for flexibility; costs 13-33% additional compute beyond pretraining.
